reason: The hypothesis transfers the Hf-coating/HfO2 barrier concept from oxidation protection of HEA substrates (P7, P9, P12) to molten-aluminum corrosion protection of boride-based components, a new application not proposed in any passage. It combines this with the finding that Hf-rich borides have better oxidation resistance (P15, P16) to justify the intervention, but the specific mechanism for molten-Al corrosion and the proposed surface enrichment treatment are not described in the literature.
copied_elements: Hf coating forms dense HfO2 protective layer (P7, P9, P12)
HfO2 reduces oxidation by acting as a barrier (P7, P9, P12)
Hf and Zr improve oxidation resistance in borides (P15, P16)
large compositional design space for tuning oxidation resistance (P17)
